title: Classification and phylogeny
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AQA A-level Biology (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EV06a#t1 term and clue written for the game; EV06a#t3 term and clue written for the game; EV06a#t2 term and clue written for the game; EV06b#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EV06a#N.7, EV06b#N.3, EV06a#N.9, EV06a#N.12.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Taxon
items.clue: Any one group in the hierarchy, such as a family or an order

items.label: Genus
items.clue: First word of a scientific name, written with a capital letter

items.label: Binomial system
items.clue: Linnaeus's scheme giving every species a universal two-part name

items.label: Common ancestor
items.clue: Shared more recently by relatives whose base sequences show fewer differences

questions.stem: Which statement about the scientific name of the tiger, Panthera tigris, is correct?

options.text: The second word, tigris, is on its own enough to identify the species of tiger.
It should be written Panthera Tigris, because both of its words are proper nouns.
Panthera names the genus and tigris distinguishes the species within it.
Panthera tigris and Panthera leo are varieties of one species and interbreed freely.

questions.explanation: First word, genus; second word, the species within that genus. Panthera leo, the lion, shares the genus and has similar traits.

questions.stem: Using the cytochrome c data, which conclusion is best supported?

options.text: Humans evolved from chimpanzees, because their cytochrome c sequences are identical.
Humans share a more recent common ancestor with the dog than with the tuna.
The tuna is the least evolved of these animals, because its protein differs most from ours.
The dog and the chicken differ from each other at 2 positions, since 13 − 11 = 2.

questions.explanation: 11 differences against 21. Differences accumulate after lineages split, so fewer differences mean a more recent common ancestor.

questions.stem: What is the main advantage of a classification in which every group corresponds to evolutionary relationships?

options.text: The groups show which of the organisms are the most advanced.
Every species is given a unique name made up of two parts.
Organisms that look alike are placed together for identification.
Characteristics of members of a group can be predicted.

questions.explanation: When all members of a group evolved from one common ancestor, they share inherited features, so a member's features can be predicted.

questions.stem: The raven is Corvus corax, the rook is Corvus frugilegus and the magpie is Pica pica. What can be concluded from these names alone?

options.text: Raven and rook are two species of one genus, likely closer to each other than to the magpie.
The raven and the rook are one species, because the first word of their names, Corvus, is the same.
The word corax on its own is enough to name the raven in any country and in any language.
The first words say nothing about how the birds are related, so only the second words are needed.
